title: Live-cell imaging and analysis of actin-mediated mitochondrial fission
protocol: Prepare the cells for imaging.
Rinse the glass-bottom dish with 1.5 mL of PBS three times.
Seed the cells with 2.0 × 10^5 cells per dish in 2 mL of total medium volume.
Incubate the cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 16 hours.
Knock down DRP1 expression using siRNA transfection according to manufacturer instructions.
Dilute siRNA by mixing 3 μL of siRNA (10 μM in stock) with 150 μL of OptiMEM for each 35 mm glass-bottom dish.

Dilute Lipofectamine RNAiMAX by mixing 9 μL of Lipofectamine RNAiMAX with 150 μL of OptiMEM for each 150 μL of diluted siRNA solution prepared in step 2-a and 150 μL of diluted Lipofectamine RNAiMAX from step 2-b, then incubate the mixture for 5 minutes at 20°C.
Add 250 μL of the combined mixture to the cells incubated on a 35 mm glass-bottom dish, and gently swirl for 2 seconds to mix solutions.
Incubate the treated cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 16 hours.
Add 125 μL of the plasmid solution (GFP-GJA1-20K and LifeAct-mCherry) per dish with incubated cells.
Gently swirl the mixture for 2 seconds.
Incubate the transfected cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 16 hours.
Warm up the culture media and imaging media at 37°C in a water bath.
Dilute Mitotracker to a final concentration of 200 nM with warmed culture media.
Incubate the dish at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 20 minutes.
Gently wash out Mitotracker by rinsing twice with imaging media.
Final volume of imaging media should be 2 mL per dish.
Set up the imaging incubator connected to the stage of the confocal microscope.
Set the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Set the excitation laser power at 50% of 488 nm for GFP.
Set the excitation laser power at 80% of 561 nm for LifeAct-mCherry.
Set the excitation laser power at 40% of 647 nm for Mitotracker Deep Red.
Set the exposure time for 100 ms for all channels.
Focus a 100× oil immersion objective on a cell with well-distributed mitochondria.
Capture image stacks at the same z-depth over time.
Obtain time-lapse images every 3 seconds, capturing three 100 ms images per acquisition.
Image for a total duration of 3 to 5 minutes.
Capture approximately 10 to 20 areas containing one to three cells each per dish.
Maintain channel settings (laser power and exposure time) between different samples.
Confirm the focal plane is at the fission point to capture full fission events.
